# HTTP integration (`pyrunner_integrations.http`)

Call any HTTP API through an HTTP API connection: an API key, a bearer token or a username and password.

Paths are relative to the connection's base URL (a full URL works too; the
credentials only go to the base URL). Each function returns the reply's body:
the parsed JSON for a JSON reply, the text for any other, None when it is empty.
A 4xx or 5xx reply raises `IntegrationError`.

An OAuth connection (Google, Microsoft 365, GitHub, Slack or Notion) works too
when you pass its name, for an endpoint PyRun has no integration for. For example:

```python
files = http.get("/drive/v3/files", connection="google")
```

Its access token goes as a bearer token only to that provider's base URL
(`https://www.googleapis.com` for Google; another host, even another Google
one, gets the request without it), and PyRun refreshes it when it expires.

## Connection

It uses a connection of the **HTTP API** kind (provider `http`), which signs in with an API key, a bearer token or a username and password. Add one under **Connections** in the sidebar and grant it to the script. Every function takes `connection=`: the connection's name, or nothing for the script's one `http` connection.

The credentials go only to the connection's base URL; a redirect elsewhere goes on without them.

## Example

```python
from pyrunner_integrations import http

# The script's one HTTP API connection (or pass connection="name").
me = http.get("/v1/me")
print("Signed in as", me["name"])

created = http.post("/v1/items", json={"name": "Ada"})

for item in http.paginate("/v1/items", items="data", cursor="next_cursor", cursor_param="cursor"):
    print(item["id"])
```

## Functions

### get

```python
http.get(path, *, connection=None, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None)
```

GET `path` and return the reply's body.

For example:

```python
user = http.get("/v1/me")
page = http.get("/v1/items", params={"page": 2})
```

### post

```python
http.post(path, *, connection=None, json=None, data=None, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None)
```

POST `json` (or form `data`) to `path` and return the reply's body.

For example:

```python
created = http.post("/v1/items", json={"name": "Ada"})
```

### put

```python
http.put(path, *, connection=None, json=None, data=None, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None)
```

PUT `json` (or `data`) to `path` and return the reply's body.

### patch

```python
http.patch(path, *, connection=None, json=None, data=None, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None)
```

PATCH `path` with `json` (or `data`) and return the reply's body.

### delete

```python
http.delete(path, *, connection=None, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None)
```

DELETE `path` and return the reply's body (often None).

### request

```python
http.request(method, path, *, connection=None, params=None, json=None, data=None, headers=None, timeout=None)
```

Send `method` to `path` and return the reply's body.

`params` go in the query string, `json` is sent as JSON, `data` as a
form (a dict) or as is (text or bytes). `headers` are added to the
connection's own. GET, PUT and DELETE are retried after a 5xx reply or a lost
connection; POST and PATCH only after a 429 or a 503 with Retry-After (any
other failure might have happened after the service acted).

### paginate

```python
http.paginate(path, *, connection=None, items='items', cursor=None, cursor_param=None, link=False, page_param=None, params=None, limit=None)
```

Yield every item of a paginated list at `path`, fetching pages as it goes.

`items` is the key of the list in each reply (dotted for a nested one,
None when the reply is the list). Pick how the API pages: `cursor="next"`
(the reply's key holding the next page's cursor, sent back as
`cursor_param`, by default the same name), `link=True` (a Link header,
like GitHub's) or `page_param="page"` (page numbers until an empty page).
`limit` stops after that many items. For example:

```python
for item in http.paginate("/v1/items", items="data", cursor="next_cursor", cursor_param="cursor"):
    print(item["id"])
```

### client

```python
http.client(connection=None, *, timeout=30)
```

The shared client of `connection`, for anything the other functions don't cover.

Its `request(method, path, ...)` returns the reply itself (`status_code`,
`headers`, `content`, `text`, `json()`); `get`/`post`/`put`/
`patch`/`delete` and `paginate` work as the functions of this module.

## Errors

Every function raises `pyrunner_integrations.IntegrationError` (a `pyrunner_connections.ConnectionsError`, so one `except` catches both) with `code`, `status` (the HTTP status, or None) and `retry_after` (seconds, or None). Its message never holds the connection's credentials. Before raising, the client retries a 429 (or a 503 with Retry-After) up to 3 times, waiting what the service asks (up to 60 s; longer, and the error says it in `retry_after`) or else 1, 2 or 4 seconds; other 5xx replies and lost connections only for GET, PUT, DELETE and other calls that are safe to repeat. After a 401 it asks PyRun once for new credentials (an OAuth token is refreshed then) and tries again.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | The service refused the request as malformed (HTTP 400, 405 or 422). |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | The service refused the credentials (HTTP 401), also after PyRun was asked for new ones. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | The account may not do this (HTTP 403): a missing scope or permission. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | No such thing (HTTP 404 or 410). |
| `CONFLICT` | It clashes with the current state (HTTP 409 or 412). |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Too many requests (HTTP 429), still after the retries; `retry_after` says when to try again. |
| `HTTP_ERROR` | Any other 4xx reply. |
| `SERVER_ERROR` | The service failed (HTTP 5xx), still after the retries. |
| `UNREACHABLE` | The service couldn't be reached (DNS, refused connection, TLS). |
| `TIMEOUT` | No reply in time. |
| `BAD_RESPONSE` | A reply that can't be used: broken JSON, too many redirects or pages, a repeated page cursor. |
| `NOT_HTTP` | The connection isn't an HTTP connection (an SMTP login). |
| `CONNECTION_...` | The connection can't be used: `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `CONNECTION_EXPIRED`... (see [Connections](../run-context.md#connections)). |
